strategies.name: T1136.002 Detection Strategy - Domain Account Creation Across Platforms

analytics.name: Analytic 0006
analytics.guidance: Adversary uses built-in tools such as 'net user /add /domain' or PowerShell to create a domain user account. The behavior chain includes: (1) suspicious process execution on a domain controller followed by (2) user account creation event (Event ID 4720) on the same host.

tuning.description: Detection triggers when Event ID 4720 follows a suspicious process within 2 minutes.
Allow filtering of known admin tools vs adversarial misuse (e.g., net.exe, powershell.exe).
Filter accounts with domain admin privileges creating new users vs standard helpdesk roles.
Restrict to only domain controller hosts to reduce noise from workstations.

analytics.name: Analytic 0007
analytics.guidance: Adversary with access to domain management tools (e.g., `realmd`, `samba-tool`, `ldapmodify`) creates a new domain user via command-line utilities. Behavior chain: LDAP command or script triggers → user entry added in AD via Kerberos/LDAP traffic.

tuning.description: realmd, samba-tool, ldapmodify or custom script
Expected Kerberos traffic from new domain account within X minutes of command
Script execution from interactive shell vs scheduled task

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: execution of realmd, samba-tool, or ldapmodify with user-related arguments

log_sources.name: NSM:Flow
log_sources.channel: TGS-REQ and AS-REQ seen for new user shortly after domain-modifying process

analytics.name: Analytic 0008
analytics.guidance: macOS clients joined to AD via LDAP may script account provisioning via `dsconfigad`, `dscl`, or LDAP scripts. Detection occurs when such tools run on a domain-joined system, followed by authentication attempts by a previously unseen account.

tuning.description: Only flag on AD-bound systems with valid LDAP context
Distinguish between user accounts and computer accounts

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: dsconfigad or dscl with create or append options for AD-bound users
